# Literature Review: Burnout and Quality of Nursing Care

> Converter test fixture only. The references below are fictitious formatting examples, not evidence.

## 1. Introduction and Rationale

The literature suggests that **burnout** is *associated with* lower quality of care (Smith & Lee, 2020); this does not establish causation. Most studies used the `MBI-HSS`. One Arabic-language study (العتيبي, 2022) reported similar patterns.

## 2. Evidence Matrix

| ID | Author/Year | Design | Sample | Key finding |
|---|---|:---:|:---:|---|
| S1 | Smith & Lee (2020) | Cross-sectional | 412 | Moderate negative association |
| S2 | العتيبي (2022) | Cross-sectional | 230 | Not reported |

## 3. Research Gaps

1. Methodological gap: few longitudinal studies.
2. Contextual gap: limited evidence from the Arab region.
   - Most samples come from a single hospital.

## References
